title: Determinism capture and replay test apply the shared command stream at different ticks
evidence:
tests/test_sim_base.gd: "## tests/test_sim_replay.gd and tools/determinism_log.gd so the committed
## capture and its sibling test can never drift apart." | tests/test_sim_replay.gd: "		if t == 120:" | tools/determinism_log.gd: "		if t == ticks / 3:" (REPLAY_TICKS=900, so commands land at tick 300) | captures/05-replay-determinism.txt: "traffic carried: 10 packets delivered across the run" | tests/test_sim_replay.gd: "check(carried >= 12, \"replay scenario carries real traffic (%d delivered — pin is not vacuous)\" % carried)" and "check(a.dump_state() != b.dump_state(), \"same command at a different tick diverges (timing is state)\")"
detail: The shared definition covers only the command list; application ticks differ (120 vs 300) and the diff itself declares timing is state — the committed capture and the sibling test are different runs, as their divergent delivered counts (10 vs ≥12) prove.
recommended_fix: Hoist the apply tick into test_sim_base (e.g. REPLAY_CMD_TICK := 120) and use that one constant in both test_sim_replay.gd and tools/determinism_log.gd.

title: Diff ships E2 tests/docs/captures but none of the sim implementation its own spec declares
evidence: spec Code Map: "+- `scripts/sim/sim_balance.gd` -- NEW: all tunables as const data (tiers, classes, lanes, ladder, speeds, queue depths, SLA thresholds, colors)" / "+- `scripts/sim/sim_core.gd` -- NEW: RefCounted deterministic sim: state, owned RNG, Dijkstra+ECMP routing, per-tick step (spawn → serialize/admit → traverse → arrive → SLA), command bus, fnv1a-32 state hash + canonical dump" / "+- `scripts/capture_runner.gd` + `captures/` -- EDIT: packets-flowing, QoS-panel, determinism log, editor-preview shots" — while tests in this diff call undefined symbols: "+func make_sim(seed_value := SEED) -> SimCore:" and "+	var sim = scene.get(\"sim\")"
detail: Every script the Code Map marks NEW/EDIT (sim_core, sim_balance, flow_view, qos_panel, main, input_router, pipe_arc, node_site, connect_controller, capture_runner) is absent from this diff; the tests cannot compile or pass against it alone.
recommended_fix: Land the scripts/ implementation in the same change, or record the chunk dependency explicitly; this diff alone cannot pass its own runner.

title: Spec change-log entry predates the spec's own creation date
evidence:
frontmatter: "+created: '2026-09-05'" vs change log: "+- 2026-09-04 (step-04 review, patch class): hash wording fixed — the code's
+  state hash is FNV-1a 32-bit"; deferred-work.md header: "## From packet-plumber-3d-e2-flow-qos step-04 review (2026-09-04)"
detail: The spec claims creation on 2026-09-05 yet records a change made 2026-09-04 — the log predates the document. Provenance dates contradict each other within one file.
recommended_fix: Correct the created date (the GDD and deferred-work both date this work 2026-09-04) or redate the change-log entry.

title: 'byte-identical' preview pin actually performs approximate float comparison
evidence:
check(_same(boot_positions, regen_positions), "regenerate reproduces the boot world byte-identically") — while _same implements: "+	for i in pa.size():
+		if not pa[i].is_equal_approx(pb[i]):
+			return false" and _staging captures only "+	return {"planet_children": planet.get_child_count(), "site_count": sites.size(), "positions": pos}"
detail: is_equal_approx tolerates float drift and the snapshot omits everything but positions and child counts — the assertion is materially weaker than its 'byte-identical' message claims.
recommended_fix: Compare exact component equality (==), or reword the message to 'identical staging (approximate float compare)'.

title: Unbounded per-stream RNG salt counters shipped; stream coupling deferred to E3
evidence:
"- [defer] Demand-stream salt bands drift into each other over very long runs
  (destination salt 7_000_000 + counter*31337 grows unboundedly; after ~1M
  spawns/house it can cross other draw bands → statistical (NOT determinism)
  coupling between seeded streams)."
detail: Long-run statistical independence of the 'owned' seed-derived streams is knowingly broken at high spawn counts; only replay byte-identity is protected. Documented, but the guard is cheap.
recommended_fix: Apply the note's own guard now (bound the counter, e.g. counter % 8192) instead of waiting for E3 demand retuning.

title: Deactivation 'still flows' check is polluted by natural demand
evidence:
# And they still FLOW: after enough ticks everything delivers (no silent loss).
+	drive(sim, 1800)
+	var accounted := int(sim.sla["email"].delivered) + int(sim.sla["email"].dropped)
+	check(accounted >= SimBalance.QUEUE_DEPTH, "deactivation: every packet accounted (delivered+dropped = %d >= %d)" % [accounted, SimBalance.QUEUE_DEPTH]) — staged endpoints 1 and 2 are houses per test_sim_base's map "[router, h, h, h, h, h, h, h, h, router, h]"; the same file's other test notes: "+	# Router endpoints (0, 9) — routers never spawn natural demand, so the
+	# observed in-flight order is purely the staged packets."
detail: During 1800 ticks natural house 1↔2 email inflates sla delivered, so 'accounted >= QUEUE_DEPTH' can pass even if the staged packets are silently lost — the safety net cannot attribute delivery.
recommended_fix: Stage on router endpoints (0,9) as _serialization_order_direct does, or tally only the staged packet ids.

title: Delivered-count pins in test_sim_flow count natural demand despite the OD-filter claim
evidence: header: "+## origin-destination pair so natural demand cannot pollute the pins." — but the pins count sim-wide: "+	check(int(r1.sim.sla["email"].delivered) > 30, "ECMP diamond delivers (%d; the flood saturates by design)" % r1.sim.sla["email"].delivered)" and "+	check(int(sim.sla["email"].delivered) > 25, "min-cost scenario delivers (%d; flood saturates by design)" % sim.sla["email"].delivered)"
detail: The OD filter applies to in-flight observation only; sla delivered counts are sim-wide, so natural house-to-house email inflates these non-vacuity thresholds — exactly what the header claims cannot happen.
recommended_fix: Derive delivered counts from staged packet ids, or stage on routers; scope the header's pollution claim to in-flight observations.

title: Serialization wave-2 ordering check passes vacuously once wave-1 email delivers
evidence:
+	check(int(inflight2[inflight2.size() - 1]) == be_id and inflight2.find(be_id) > inflight2.find(email_id),
+		"serialization: Best-effort admits after the higher lanes (tail = %d)" % int(inflight2[inflight2.size() - 1])) — after "drive(sim, 3)" a second time, wave-1 packets may no longer be in flight
detail: find(email_id) returns -1 when the wave-1 email has already delivered; then any non-negative index for be_id satisfies the comparison — the Best-effort-ordering property is unproven on that path.
recommended_fix: Precondition on inflight2.find(email_id) >= 0, or assert ordering via recorded admission order instead of in-flight positions.
